editorial:
Imagine being a huge star who the world completely forgot about. That is exactly where you find Norma Desmond, a former movie icon who is stuck in the past and desperate to get back on screen. Then you have a broke writer who just needs a place to stay and a way to make some money. When these two meet, it starts off as a simple deal, but it quickly turns into something way more intense. The vibe is moody and tense, making you feel like something is wrong from the very first scene. You will feel for the writer as he gets pulled deeper into Norma's strange world, where the line between reality and fame gets blurry.

What really makes this version work is the acting, which feels raw and real. The pacing is tight, so you never feel bored, though some parts might feel a bit too heavy if you are looking for a light comedy. If you love stories about the dark side of fame, you need to see this. For the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the detail. If you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great call because the colors and sound are just that good.
endingExplained: Things fall apart when the writer tries to leave Norma to start a real life. Norma cannot handle being rejected, so she kills him in a fit of rage. In the final scene, she has completely lost touch with reality. She thinks the police and news cameras are there to film her big comeback movie. She walks down the stairs for her final close-up, totally delusional and broken as she is taken away.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about fame and obsession.
